subject.title: exec auto-reviewer re-bills a fresh model completion for every byte-identical repeated exec

question: May OpenClaw reuse model-backed exec reviewer decisions for byte-identical exec requests, and what exact cache lifetime/key shape should define that reuse?
rationale: The source-level cost bug is clear, but skipping a fresh model review for a later exec request changes exec approval semantics and needs explicit approval-boundary intent.

options.title: Approve per-reviewer full-input memo
options.body: Cache parsed reviewer decisions only inside one createModelExecAutoReviewer instance, keyed by the full reviewed input or prompt including host and agent/session context, with no persistence or durable approval conversion.

options.title: Cache low-risk allow-once only
options.body: Reuse only low-risk allow-once decisions while continuing to re-review ask, timeout, and error outcomes, reducing behavior change at the cost of less dedupe.

options.title: Keep one-request-one-review semantics
options.body: Accept repeated reviewer completion cost until maintainers decide a fresh model review is required for every exec request.

recommendation.title: Approve per-reviewer full-input memo
recommendation.body: Cache parsed reviewer decisions only inside one createModelExecAutoReviewer instance, keyed by the full reviewed input or prompt including host and agent/session context, with no persistence or durable approval conversion.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and recent merged PR metadata make this the strongest available owner for the approval-boundary decision.
